row.reason: Both are investor-owned, rate-regulated electric and natural gas utilities that own and operate delivery networks and bill residential, commercial and industrial customers directly. They serve different regions, so they don't compete for the same customers. Con Edison also sells steam and has a transmission investment arm, and Avista also owns generation. Those differences are minor next to the shared core business.

T:P2.3.text: Con Edison's principal business segments are Consolidated Edison Company of New York, a regulated electric, gas, and steam utility; Orange & Rockland Utilities (O&R), a regulated electric and gas utility; and Con Edison Transmission, Inc.

T:P2.4.text: Con Edison of New York provides electric service to multiple million customers and gas service to multiple million customers in New York City and Westchester County. The company also provides steam service in parts of Manhattan. Visit Con Edison’s website.

T:P2.5.text: Orange & Rockland provides electric service to multiple customers in southeastern New York and adjacent areas of northern New Jersey and gas service to multiple customers in southeastern New York. Visit Orange & Rockland’s website.

T:P2.6.text: Con Edison Transmission invests in electric and natural gas transmission projects that offer customers access to diverse, low-cost energy supplies. Visit Con Edison Transmission’s website.

C:S1.1.text: Avista Corporation is an investor-owned utility headquartered in Spokane, Washington, and its regulated business unit is Avista Utilities. The company also owns Alaska Electric Light & Power, which provides electric services in Juneau, Alaska.

C:S2.1.text: Avista Utilities provides electric distribution and transmission services and natural gas distribution in eastern Washington and northern Idaho, along with natural gas service in parts of Oregon.

C:S3.1.text: A 2020 SEC filing describes its regulated operations as spanning Washington, Idaho, Oregon and Montana.
